architecture.mechanism: Combined n-tetradecane phase-change microcapsule/polyurethane (PCMS-PUR) coating plus electrothermal heating induces interfacial softening and a lubricating meltwater layer in saline ice, causing whole-block sliding detachment rather than progressive melting.
architecture.intervention: Coat offshore wind turbine blade leading edges with an n-tetradecane PCMS-PUR coating and embed electrothermal heaters operated at 8–12 kW/m² heat flux, so the phase-change buffering plus heating softens the saline ice interface under salt spray and high wind.
architecture.expected_effect: Saline ice detaches as whole blocks via interfacial sliding, lowering de-icing energy demand and ice adhesion in cold marine environments, thereby restoring winter power output while the polyurethane matrix resists saline droplet exposure and wind loading.
architecture.falsification_test: Test a GFRP blade section in a recirculating low-temperature icing wind tunnel at 3% salinity, −5/−10/−15 °C, 3/6/9 m/s wind, 60 mL/min water flow, 0.3 MPa spray; if no interfacial meltwater layer forms, ice fails to detach by whole-block sliding, energy consumption exceeds the freshwater baseline, or the coating delaminates/erodes under saline spray and high wind, the mechanism is falsified.
